metadata.title: Your Targeted Nanoparticle Doesn't Reach More Tumor. It Just Enters More Cells.
metadata.purpose: vox-explainer of Cancer Nanomedicine candidate 03. One claim: uptake does not equal accumulation, because the targeting ligand acts only at the last step.
metadata.color_semantics: TEAL = particle accumulation in tumor / what's actually measured; CRIMSON = cell uptake / the last-step-only action; GOLD = the binding step
metadata.note: EXCLUSIONS: protein corona (own video), EC145-vs-mirvetuximab case, the 0.7% figure, EPR's contested status. One claim only: uptake does not equal accumulation, because the ligand acts last.

props.command: What is: Your targeted nanoparticle doesn't reach more tumor. It just enters more cells?

beats.narration_text: This is Liam, in for Bear. Your targeted nanoparticle — decorated with antibodies — binds cancer cells ten times better in a dish. In the animal, both particles reach the tumor in nearly equal amounts.

props.title: In a dish vs in the animal

items.label: In the dish
items.sub: Antibody-decorated particles bind cancer cells 10× better

items.label: In the animal
items.sub: Targeted and untargeted reach the tumor in nearly equal amounts

items.label: The gap
items.sub: Culture-side win doesn't translate to tumor delivery

beats.narration_text: The antibody works beautifully in the lab. The tumor data tells a different story. The targeting ligand made almost no difference to how much drug reached the tumor.

items.label: In the lab
items.sub: The antibody works beautifully — strong binding to cancer cells

items.label: In the tumor
items.sub: Ligand made almost no difference to delivered drug

items.label: The disconnect
items.sub: Same molecule — one win, one no-effect — depending on where you measure

beats.narration_text: A ligand that binds cells ten times better in culture — yet doesn't increase how much drug reaches the tumor. The ligand is working. Why doesn't it help?
A nanoparticle travels through a chain of environments to reach a cancer cell: blood, tumor vessel wall, tumor tissue — then, finally, the cell surface. Targeting acts only at the very last step.

items.label: 1. Blood
items.sub: Nanoparticle circulates in the bloodstream

items.label: 2. Vessel wall
items.sub: Crosses out of the tumor's blood vessel

items.label: 3. Tumor tissue
items.sub: Diffuses through the tumor interstitium

items.label: 4. Cell surface — ligand acts HERE
items.sub: Targeting engages only at the very last step

beats.narration_text: Cell culture measures only step four — binding and entry — in conditions with no circulation, no vessel walls, no clearance. It cannot tell you what happens at steps one through three.

props.title: What a plate assay can and can't see

items.label: What culture measures
items.sub: Step 4 only — binding and entry, in a dish

items.label: What culture removes
items.sub: No circulation, no vessel walls, no clearance

items.label: The blind spot
items.sub: Steps 1–3 are invisible to the assay you ran

beats.narration_text: Total tumor accumulation is set by two earlier steps: how long the particle survives in circulation, and how permeable the tumor's blood vessels are. The ligand touches neither.

items.label: Circulation half-life
items.sub: How long the particle survives before it is cleared

items.label: Vessel permeability
items.sub: How leaky the tumor's blood vessels are

items.label: The ligand
items.sub: Touches neither — accumulation is set before it acts

beats.narration_text: The ligand acts only after the particle has already arrived — at the cell surface, improving internalization. It cannot go back upstream and fix accumulation.

props.title: The ligand's moment of action — after arrival

items.label: What the ligand does
items.sub: At the cell surface — improves internalization once the particle arrives

items.label: What it can't do
items.sub: Cannot go back upstream to fix accumulation

items.label: Sequence matters
items.sub: Ligand acts after arrival — never before then

beats.narration_text: If accumulation is the bottleneck — too few particles reach the tumor — fixing cellular uptake does not help. You're improving the last step when the problem is upstream.

props.title: Wrong fix — improving step 4 while step 1 is the choke

items.label: If the bottleneck is upstream
items.sub: Too few particles reach the tumor at all

items.label: Fixing uptake won't help
items.sub: You are improving the last step of the chain

items.label: Match the fix to the choke
items.sub: Diagnose accumulation before you optimize binding

beats.narration_text: Two batches: folate-targeted and bare. Equal dose injected. Four hours later — tumor accumulation: 2.1% vs 1.9%. Nearly identical. But cellular internalization: 68% vs 12%. Same tumor, different cell entry.

items.label: Tumor accumulation
items.sub: Targeted 2.1% vs bare 1.9% — nearly identical (illustrative)

items.label: Cellular internalization
items.sub: Targeted 68% vs bare 12% — very different (illustrative)

items.label: Same tumor, different cell entry
items.sub: The ligand moved uptake, not accumulation

beats.narration_text: Binds cells in a dish is not reaches a tumor in a body. The ligand acts last. Total accumulation is set upstream — by circulation and vessel permeability, not by binding.

items.label: In a dish ≠ in a body
items.sub: Binding is not delivery

items.label: The ligand acts last
items.sub: Only at step 4 — the cell surface

items.label: Fix upstream
items.sub: Circulation half-life and vessel permeability — not binding

beats.narration_text: The verdict. A targeting ligand that binds cancer cells ten times better in a dish will not, by itself, increase how much drug reaches a tumor in an animal. Accumulation is set upstream — by circulation half-life and vessel permeability. The ligand acts only at the last step, at the cell surface, and improves cellular internalization once the particle has already arrived. Fix the bottleneck, or the fix does not help.
